conceptTag: A software tool: direct or through partners?
readerTitle: A van dealer wants to sell your software. Who gets the customer?
caseNote: 가상 사례 (배송 경로 소프트웨어, 포장기 제조사) · 모든 수치는 설명용
insight: 파트너 채널은 수수료가 아니라 계약이 끝난 뒤 고객 관계가 누구에게 남는지로 판단한다.
misconception: 파트너가 대신 팔아 주면 수수료만 내면 되고, 고객은 어차피 내 제품을 쓰니 내 고객이다.

sources.text: 모든 수치와 사례는 설명용 가상 예시

factChecks.note: 계산 확인: 월 구독료 $100 − 딜러 몫 30% $30 = 회사 몫 $70. 모든 수치는 설명용 가상 수치입니다.
관련 개념 레슨(MKT-06-04 파트너 채널, MKT-06-06 고객 소유)의 정의와 표현이 이 레슨의 요약과 일치하는지 확인하세요.

cards.title: A van dealer wants to sell your software.
body: Two founders built a route-planning app for small delivery fleets. It saves drivers about an hour a day. Finding fleet owners has been slow.
Then a regional van dealer calls. They sell hundreds of vans a year to exactly those owners, and they want to offer the app with every van.

image.label: A van on a dealer lot with a phone showing a route map
image.brief: 3D 클레이 스타일. 상용 밴 판매장에 밴 한 대가 서 있고, 앞유리에 경로 지도가 뜬 휴대폰이 붙어 있음. 판매원과 고객이 악수하는 장면. 실제 자동차 브랜드 로고나 앱 로고는 쓰지 않음.

cards.title: The dealer's offer
body: The app costs $100 a month. The dealer would sign customers up, bill them, and keep 30%. They also ask to be your only seller in the region.

options.text: Sign as offered. The dealer reaches far more fleets than you can
options.feedback: You gain reach fast, but the dealer holds the billing and the relationship. That's **owning the customer**, and you'd be giving it away along with your region.
You keep every customer and every dollar, but you skip a **partner channel** that already meets your buyers at the exact moment they buy a van.

options.text: Take the deal, but customers create accounts with you and you bill them
options.feedback: The dealer brings trust and timing, and you keep the account. You use the partner as a channel without handing over the customer.

cards.title: The 30% is not the real question.
body: The dealer's cut is easy to see. The harder question is who the fleet owner calls when a route breaks, and who they renew with next year.

breakdown.label: Dealer share
breakdown.detail: Pays for the sale and the trust

breakdown.label: Left for you
breakdown.detail: With no cost to find the customer

cards.title: Why this partner fits
body: From **Partners as channels**: a good partner already has your buyers' attention and trust, and reaches them at the moment the need is sharpest.
A fleet owner buying a van is already thinking about routes, drivers and fuel. A salesperson they trust says, "Most buyers add this." The founders could never create that moment by cold-calling.

cards.title: Whoever bills them, owns them.
body: From **Owning the customer**: the business that holds the account, the contact details and the bill holds the relationship.

If the dealer bills, the founders can't offer a bigger plan, can't hear complaints early, and can't keep customers if the dealer switches to a rival app next year. The product would be theirs. The customers would not.

image.label: Two arrows: customer linked to dealer, or linked to the app maker
image.brief: 두 개의 도식을 나란히. 왼쪽: 고객 → 딜러 → 앱 회사 (고객과 앱 회사 사이 연결 없음). 오른쪽: 딜러가 고객을 소개하고, 고객과 앱 회사가 굵은 선으로 직접 연결됨. 로고 없이 단순한 아이콘.

cards.title: One clause to fight for
body: The dealer agrees to talk terms but will only bend on one point. Which do you push for?

options.feedback: More money per sale, but the dealer still holds every account. You win the margin and lose the relationship.

options.text: Customers sign up and pay through your app; the dealer earns a referral fee
options.feedback: This keeps you **owning the customer** while the dealer still gets paid for the trust it brings. Renewals and upgrades come to you.

options.text: Drop the exclusivity so you can add more dealers
options.feedback: More partners widen reach, but each one would still own its customers. You'd have more channels and no relationships.

cards.title: Owning the customer has a price.
body: If customers come to you, so do their support calls, billing problems and late payments. Two founders may not be ready for that.
Partners also earn their share. If you squeeze the dealer too hard, their sales team stops mentioning you. A referral fee that feels small to them buys you very little effort.

cards.title: Now it's a machine maker.
body: You build pallet-wrapping machines for warehouses. A warehouse equipment distributor wants to carry them. It visits about 2,000 warehouses a year.
How do you set it up?

options.text: Hand the distributor everything: sales, service and warranty records
options.feedback: Easy to start, but you'd never learn who uses your machines. If the distributor adds a rival brand, those buyers go with it.

options.text: Use the distributor to sell, but warranty registration and spare parts come to you
options.feedback: The **partner channel** brings reach and trust, and registration gives you a direct line to each buyer. You keep the customer without doing the selling.

options.text: Decline and hire your own sales reps
options.feedback: You own every customer, but reaching 2,000 warehouses alone would take years and cost far more than the distributor's margin.

cards.title: Borrow the partner's reach. Keep the customer.
body: Two ideas did the work here. **Partners as channels** showed when a partner reaches buyers better than you can. **Owning the customer** showed what to protect in the deal.
**Try it today:** for each way you sell, write down who holds the customer's contact details and who sends the bill.
